chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Transformer Architecture and Self‑Attention
chapters.description: Covers the core Transformer building blocks and the mathematics of self‑attention that underlie modern large language models (LLMs). Establishes notation for queries, keys, values, attention weights, and the forward pass used throughout the literature.
subtopics: Overview of encoder/decoder and decoder‑only Transformer variants
Multi‑head self‑attention: queries, keys, values, and heads
Attention computation: softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V
Positional dependence in attention and why positional information is required
Residual connections, layer normalization, and feed‑forward blocks
Computational complexity (O(n^2) attention) and memory considerations
Common modifications used in LLMs (causal attention, rotary attention hooks)

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Positional Representations in Sequence Models
chapters.description: Introduces why positional information is needed in Transformers and surveys standard approaches to encoding token positions, including absolute, relative, learned, and sinusoidal encodings.
subtopics: Why positional encodings are necessary for Transformers
Absolute positional encodings: learned embeddings and sinusoidal encodings
Relative positional encodings and bias methods
Pros/cons of learned vs analytic (sinusoidal) encodings
How positional encodings interact with attention (additive vs multiplicative)
Evaluation considerations: extrapolation vs interpolation of position encodings

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)
chapters.description: Detailed treatment of rotary (RoPE) embeddings: their mathematical formulation as rotations applied to token representations, parameterization of rotary angles, implementation details, and properties important for extrapolation.
subtopics: Derivation of RoPE as complex (2D) rotations on sub‑vectors
Rotary angle parameterization: theta_i and base values (e.g., 10000)
Mapping from position index n to cos(n theta_i), sin(n theta_i) pairs
How RoPE integrates with Q/K (multiplicative application) and invariances
Frequency interpretation of RoPE dimensions (high vs low frequency dims)
Implementation considerations (efficient routines, interleaving cos/sin)
Behavior of RoPE under position scaling and implications for extrapolation

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Strategies for Extending Context Windows via Positional Interpolation
chapters.description: Examines prior methods used to extend model context length by modifying positional encodings — why they are needed, how they operate mathematically, and their empirical trade‑offs.
subtopics: Motivation: new token indices and out‑of‑distribution positional values
Linear positional interpolation (PI): downscaling position indices
NTK‑informed scaling: distributing interpolation across frequencies
Group or hybrid strategies (e.g., dividing dims by frequency and applying different rules)
Extrapolation vs interpolation: definitions and practical differences
Empirical failure modes: crowded positions, catastrophic values, short‑context degradation
When fine‑tuning is required vs non‑fine‑tuning methods

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Intuition for Positional Encoding
chapters.description: Presents the high‑level NTK perspective used to reason about how different frequency components of positional encodings affect model behavior, and why lower/higher frequency dims might be treated differently.
subtopics: Basic NTK concepts: kernel view of infinitely wide neural networks
How positional signals map to kernel behavior and receptive scales
Frequency response and NTK: why high‑frequency components behave differently
NTK‑motivated interpolation/extrapolation heuristics
Limitations and empirical interpretation of NTK in finite networks

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Language Modeling, Metrics, and Long‑Sequence Evaluation
chapters.description: Covers language modeling objectives, common evaluation metrics (especially perplexity), and practical methods for evaluating models on long documents (sliding windows, chunking).
subtopics: Next‑token prediction objective and cross‑entropy loss
Perplexity: definition, interpretation, and calculation
Sliding‑window evaluation protocols for long sequences
Chunking, overlapping windows, and aggregation of log‑probs
Task formulations for long context evaluation (e.g., passkey retrieval)
Statistical considerations: sample size, variability, and significance

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Fine‑Tuning Large Language Models and Efficient Tuning Methods
chapters.description: Discusses standard fine‑tuning processes for pre‑trained LLMs, common hyperparameters and pitfalls (catastrophic forgetting, instability), and parameter‑efficient alternatives used in practice.
subtopics: Full‑model fine‑tuning vs parameter‑efficient approaches (LoRA, adapters)
Learning rate schedules, batch size, and mixed precision
Catastrophic forgetting and regularization strategies
Dataset formatting for long‑sequence fine‑tuning (chunking, BOS/EOS bookending)
Practical fine‑tuning constraints: steps, GPU memory, and throughput
Techniques for long‑sequence fine‑tuning (gradient accumulation, checkpointing)

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Search and Optimization Methods — Evolutionary Algorithms and Genetic Search
chapters.description: Introduces evolutionary algorithms, genetic operators, population strategies, and how such methods are applied for black‑box search problems like hyperparameter tuning or discrete design choices.
subtopics: Overview of evolutionary algorithms and genetic algorithms
Encoding solutions, fitness evaluation, and selection schemes
Mutation and crossover operators and parameterization
Population initialization strategies and seeding with heuristics
Constraints and monotonicity enforcement during search
Trade-offs: exploration vs exploitation, sample efficiency, parallelism

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Signal Processing and Frequency Analysis for Positional Encodings
chapters.description: Provides core signal‑processing intuition relevant to positional encodings: frequency decomposition, aliasing, sampling effects, and why different frequency bands encode position at different granularities.
subtopics: Sinusoids as basis functions and Fourier intuition
Frequency interpretation of positional encodings
Aliasing, resolution, and sampling rate analogies for token positions
Why low‑frequency components capture long‑range orders and high‑frequency capture locality
Consequences of scaling/warping angles on information content

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Long‑Context Modeling Challenges and Complementary Approaches
chapters.description: Surveys engineering and methodological challenges unique to extreme context lengths and summarizes complementary techniques (retrieval augmentation, memory layers, streaming/online attention) that address aspects of long context.
subtopics: Data scarcity for extremely long documents and synthetic construction
Compute and memory costs of training/inference with long sequences
Attention dispersion and degraded short‑context performance
Retrieval‑augmented models and external memory modules
Streaming and recurrent attention schemes (e.g., chunked/rolling context)
Sparse and structured attention (local window, global tokens, long‑range attention)

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Efficient Attention Mechanisms and Architectures for Long Sequences
chapters.description: Details algorithmic and architectural techniques to reduce the cost of attention and enable longer contexts: sparse attention patterns, locality‑sensitive hashing, block/parallel windowing, and memory/compression strategies.
subtopics: Windowed/local attention and sliding window implementations
Global tokens, routing tokens, and hierarchical attention
Low‑rank and sketching methods for attention approximation
LSH attention and other approximate nearest neighbor approaches
Memory/compression mechanisms: summarization, key/value caching
Practical tradeoffs: accuracy vs speed vs memory

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Datasets, Data Preparation, and Practical Evaluation Protocols for Long Contexts
chapters.description: Presents common corpora and how to prepare long sequences for training and evaluation, covering datasets used in long‑context research and considerations for fair evaluation.
subtopics: Common long‑document corpora: PG19, The Pile (Books3, Pile‑Books), RedPajama, Proof‑pile
Data chunking strategies, minimum length requirements, and bookending tokens
Creating validation/test splits with sufficiently long samples
Passkey retrieval and synthetic tasks for measuring retrieval over long context
Sliding window stride, overlap choice and its effect on metrics
Reproducibility: random seeds, sample selection, and reporting

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Implementation, Numerical Stability and Inference Considerations
chapters.description: Covers practical software/hardware issues relevant to operating with RoPE and positional rescaling at inference time, including numerical precision, dynamic selection of positional strategies, and runtime performance.
subtopics: Efficient implementation of cos/sin mixes and rotary multiplications
Numerical stability at very large position indices (FP32 vs FP16/BF16)
Dynamic switching of positional encoding settings at inference (per‑length selection)
Memory/layout concerns for long sequence attention buffers
Distributed inference and GPU memory optimizations
Profiling inference latency and throughput for long inputs

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Experimental Design, Ablation Methodology and Reporting Best Practices
chapters.description: Guidance on designing experiments to evaluate long‑context methods, how to perform ablations to attribute gains, and best practices for reporting results and limitations.
subtopics: Designing controlled comparisons and baselines
Ablation types: component removal, parameter sweeps, and sensitivity analysis
Reporting metrics across multiple context lengths and datasets
Statistical variability and confidence intervals
Resource accounting (compute, GPUs, fine‑tuning steps) in results
Documenting failure modes and limitations
